items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Experience coordinating complex administrative processes involving multiple stakeholders, with the ability to track progress, follow up effectively, and ensure timely completion.
Experience administering university research programs or coordinating academic personnel processes.
Experience working with UC Berkeley, the VA, or similarly complex institutions.
Experience in VA research administration, Work Without Compensation (WOC) appointments, onboarding processes, or VA systems.

The Lab Manager will support the administration of Professor David Chan’s health economics research program, which involves personnel and projects across UC Berkeley, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and collaborating institutions.

The position requires strong organizational skills, sound judgment, and persistent follow-through. The coordinator will track administrative processes, identify obstacles, communicate with institutional offices, and help resolve issues so that research personnel can work effectively.
Personnel onboarding and appointment coordination - 30%
Coordinate recruitment and appointment logistics with Berkeley HR and academic personnel staff.
Help incoming personnel navigate Berkeley and VA onboarding, including required paperwork, training, appointments, and account provisioning.
Maintain onboarding checklists, track outstanding requirements, and follow up with personnel and institutional contacts.
Identify delays and escalate unresolved issues to the appropriate office or faculty supervisor.
Track appointment end dates, renewals, and personnel transitions.
Project and program administration - 25%
Maintain administrative timelines, task lists, and records across research projects.
Maintain staffing and funding trackers, flag projected gaps, and prepare planning scenarios with the relevant finance staff.
Coordinate meetings, document decisions, and follow up on action items.
Develop and maintain clear administrative procedures and guidance for lab personnel.
Serve as a liaison among the faculty supervisor, research staff, collaborators, and Berkeley and VA administrative offices.
Identify recurring administrative problems and recommend practical improvements, including the appropriate use of approved digital and AI tools.
Grant application and funding coordination - 20%
Help identify relevant funding opportunities and track application deadlines and requirements.
Coordinate collection of application materials, supporting documents, and collaborator information.
Work with faculty and campus research administrators on proposal preparation and submission.
Assist with administrative reporting, funding records, and follow-up on award setup, expenditures, and interinstitutional funding arrangements.
Refer budget, allowability, and award-management questions to the responsible institutional specialists.
Compliance coordination and records management - 15%
Track required training, approvals, renewals, and administrative documentation.
Coordinate with responsible offices on research compliance and personnel access requirements.
Maintain organized records and handle confidential personnel and institutional information appropriately.
Help ensure that administrative tasks are completed in accordance with established Berkeley and VA procedures.
Professional Learning and Growth - 5%
Actively contributes to a team environment that fosters a culture of belonging for all, both within the unit and at Haas.
Exemplifies Haas four Defining Leadership Principles: (1) Question the status quo; (2) Confidence without attitude; (3) Students always; and (4) Beyond yourself.
Completes required training on time and engages in opportunities for learning pertinent to the position or at the suggestion of the supervisor.
Other duties as assigned - 5%
Clear, professional written and verbal communication.
Familiarity with grant applications, sponsored research administration, or compliance coordination.
Sound judgment in handling confidential information and determining when to seek guidance.
Proficiency with spreadsheets, shared documents, and common administrative tools.
Exemplifies Haas' four Defining Leadership Principles: (1) Question the status quo; (2) Confidence without attitude; (3) Students always; and (4) Beyond yourself.
Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple processes and deadlines.

Skilled at identifying recurring bottlenecks and redesigning administrative processes, including the effective use of approved AI tools. Comfortable with, or able to learn, project tracking and documentation tools such as GitHub. This role does not require coding.
Ability to interpret procedures, identify missing information, and follow issues through to resolution.
Demonstrated ability to maintain staffing and funding trackers, identify projected gaps, and prepare planning scenarios for review in collaboration with the relevant finance staff.
Excellent interpersonal skills, demonstrating a desire to establish and maintain positive & professional working relationships with colleagues, students, and team members.
